notes: Elapsed time and memory are machine-dependent observations, not hard-coded pass criteria.
The established gate values are repeated here so threshold changes are explicit and reviewable.
The detailed phase profile remains the Phase A baseline; later gate observations show optimization progress.
The Phase O gate measures the finalized default with both XLSX and HTML enabled, so it remains comparable with the earlier phases.
Phase E adds independent --no-xlsx-output and --no-html-output controls; supplying both produces promoted CSV-only review files without weakening the row ceiling or financial assertions.
Phase F preserves every raw source-detail value while projecting non-presentation columns in bulk and classifying each presentation row once.
Phase G keeps base-currency and period-boundary assertions active in production while evaluating them with Polars expressions instead of Python row dictionaries.
Phase H reuses the FX portfolio-period index and appends lineage metadata column-wise while preserving byte-identical SHA-256 finding fingerprints.
Phase I indexes complete evidence rows once and preserves their original ordering instead of constructing a small Polars DataFrame for every changed period.
Phase J materializes each holdings and transactions snapshot union once and reuses those rows across every enabled Data Audit cross-reference check.
Phase K caches repeated source-detail wording and classification shapes while copying portfolio identity, source locator, and review key from every individual finding row.
Phase L builds each holdings-and-transactions reconstruction index once per snapshot and reuses it for separate portfolio and security Modified Dietz checks.
Phase M derives source candidates once per Modified Dietz formula input and uses the same result for effect allocation and mandatory unallocated-input visibility.
Phase N resolves each changed-value tolerance once per compared field and skips Modified Dietz external-flow eligibility for fields that cannot produce that diagnostic estimate.

Phase N's 100x profile reduced changed-value comparison from 3.55 seconds to 2.61 seconds; its single 500x wall-clock sample was 0.85 seconds slower than Phase M and is retained as measured run-to-run variation rather than reported as a gate improvement.
Phase O caches each fully validated normalized dataset/snapshot frame for one Audit run; later Audit runs reload and revalidate their inputs.

Phase O reduced normalized CSV construction from 99 executions to 12 at 100x, reduced the full 100x profile from 33.57 seconds to 29.74 seconds, and reduced the 500x wall-clock observation from 86.97 seconds to 78.50 seconds.
Phase P appends, measures, and formats workbook rows in one pass while resolving invariant date and numeric column roles once per sheet.

Phase P preserved all values and visible formatting across 410,261 generated workbook cells, reduced the full 100x profile from 29.74 seconds to 28.47 seconds, and reduced the 500x wall-clock observation from 78.50 seconds to 76.71 seconds.
Phase Q compiles exact JSON scalar encoders once per finding column and bounds repeated-value caches while preserving every persisted SHA-256 fingerprint byte.

Phase Q reduced profiled 100x finding-audit-trail construction from 1.72 seconds to 1.13 seconds; its 77.87-second 500x sample is retained as measured run-to-run variation, not reported as an aggregate gate improvement.
Phase R short-circuits empty Data Audit filters, reuses the holdings rate index, and sorts continuity rows once in Polars instead of sorting every Python group.

Phase R preserved all 2,600 profiled 100x Data Audit rows exactly and reduced x_ref processing from 2.18 seconds to 1.88 seconds; the combined Phase Q and R target paths are 0.97 seconds faster in the 100x profile.
Phase R's 77.29-second 500x sample passed the unchanged gate and remains within the observed wall-clock variation around Phase P's 76.71-second sample.

Phase S indexes eligible holdings, flow, and income rows once by Modified Dietz owner/component instead of rescanning owner rows for every formula input, and reuses cached performance-input classification.

Phase S preserved all report CSV rows and all 410,261 workbook cells and formats, reduced profiled 100x report-table derivation from 10.20 seconds to 8.82 seconds, and reduced the full profile from 29.71 seconds to 26.90 seconds.
Phase S also sorts duplicate fallback-transaction diagnostics explicitly, making findings.csv byte-identical across separate Audit processes without hiding or changing any finding.
Phase S reduced the 500x wall-clock observation from 77.29 seconds to 75.59 seconds while passing the unchanged hard gate.
Phase T evaluates matching-row deltas and tolerances in lazy Polars branches, collects only material changed-value candidates, and preserves the established row-and-field finding order.

Phase T preserved portfolio and security finding rows exactly, reduced profiled 100x changed-value detection from 2.43 seconds to 1.90 seconds, and reduced the full profile from 26.90 seconds to 25.92 seconds.
Phase T reduced the 500x wall-clock observation from 75.59 seconds to 71.87 seconds while passing the unchanged hard gate.

Phase U matches targets to related evidence, calculates priority scores, applies deterministic tie-breaks, and assigns period ranks in one lazy Polars plan while leaving financial-impact estimation unchanged.
Phase U preserved all 58,700 profiled 100x portfolio and security ranking rows in exact order and value, and every supporting CSV remained byte-identical apart from regenerated manifests.
Phase U reduced profiled 100x contribution-candidate construction from 1.57 seconds to 0.79 seconds and primary-coverage construction from 2.25 seconds to 1.53 seconds.
Phase U reduced the 500x wall-clock observation from 71.87 seconds to 66.40 seconds while passing the unchanged hard gate.
Phase V keeps mandatory SN-04 market-value continuity active in production while using grouped Polars shifts to evaluate adjacent periods and materializing only violations.
Phase V preserved all 2,600 profiled 100x x_ref rows exactly, and every supporting CSV remained byte-identical apart from regenerated manifests.
Phase V reduced profiled 100x market-value continuity processing from approximately 0.53 seconds to 0.014 seconds and total x_ref processing from 1.79 seconds to 1.28 seconds.
Phase V's required 500x gate passed at 70.10 seconds and a 69.37x ratio; the wall-clock sample is slower than Phase U's 66.40 seconds and is not reported as an aggregate improvement.

A same-process isolated 500x benchmark reduced the Phase V target path from 1.2709 seconds to 0.0572 seconds with identical issue counts, indicating an approximately 1.21-second target-path saving despite full-run timing variation.
Phase W keeps SN-01, SN-02, SN-05, and SN-07 active in production while associating finding fingerprints, assigning cause dispositions, and detecting invalid cause rows with Polars operations.
Phase W hashes each distinct economic-effect payload once and retains the exact persisted SHA-256 identifiers, owner labels, lineage fingerprints, row order, and fail-closed safety behavior.

Phase W preserved all 26,100 profiled 100x cause-lineage CSV rows byte-for-byte and every supporting CSV remained byte-identical; regenerated manifests and the temporary comparison-path string are intentionally run-specific.
Phase W reduced profiled 100x cause-lineage and conservation processing from 1.307 seconds to 0.491 seconds and the full profile from 25.616 seconds to 25.071 seconds.
Phase W reduced the 500x wall-clock observation from 70.10 seconds to 63.92 seconds while passing the unchanged hard gate; elapsed observations remain machine-dependent.
Phase measurements identify optimization targets and may include nested work; they are not additive accounting.
Financial and reviewer-facing equivalence is enforced independently by scripts/check_scale.py.
